name: Jonathan
charge: Stripping himself of his robe for the man whom the Lord would make king; and thou shalt be king, and I shall be next unto thee
summary: The king's son and heir made a covenant with the shepherd who had just killed Goliath, and gave him his robe, his garments, his sword, his bow and his girdle. He warned him of his father's intent, spoke for him and was nearly killed for it, and met him in the wood at Ziph to strengthen his hand in God. He said outright that David would be king and he himself would be next. He died with his father on Gilboa.
offense: Jonathan's confidence in the Lord preceded his covenant with David. At the Philistine garrison he declared that no restraint could keep the Lord from saving by many or by few, and went forward with his armour-bearer (1 Samuel 14:6-14). He had already risked his life for Israel when David came into the history as its champion. Their bond joined men who had acted upon the same trust. Jonathan loved David as his own soul, made a covenant with him, and gave him his robe, garments, sword, bow, and girdle (1 Samuel 18:1-4). His conduct was the opposite of Saul's envy. As David's honour increased, Jonathan did not treat another servant's calling as an injury to himself. Colossians 2:2 speaks of hearts knit together in love; shared faith strengthens service instead of dividing it by rivalry. When Saul ordered David killed, Jonathan warned him and argued his innocence before the king. David had risked his life and done Saul good; killing him without cause would shed innocent blood (1 Samuel 19:1-7). Later Saul explicitly connected David's survival to Jonathan's loss of the kingdom and threw a javelin at his own son (1 Samuel 20:30-33). Jonathan would not purchase a throne through the murder of his friend. He met David in the wood and strengthened his hand in God, acknowledging that David would be king (1 Samuel 23:16-18). The threatened man needed more than information about Saul's movements. He needed a brother who would stand with the Lord's purpose when doing so cost him advantage. Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 6:14 calls a faithful friend a strong defence; Jonathan supplied that defence in counsel, warning, and covenant.
